issues.description: Identifier mismatch for the Genre name property: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) specifies that the Genre struct should have a String property named `name` and an optional `subgenre`. In the solution implementation (Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift) the Genre struct declares the property as `genreName: String`. Meanwhile the solution's Client code and Book assembly instantiate and access the field using `Genre(name: ...)` and `genre.name` (Sources/BookstoreLib/Client.swift). This naming inconsistency will cause compilation errors in the provided solution and will confuse students who expect the field to be named `name` per the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Genre identifier consistent across artifacts. Rename the property in the Genre struct from `genreName` to `name` (let name: String) so it matches the problem statement and the existing Client/assembly usage (Genre(name: ...) and genre.name). Alternatively, update all call sites and initializers to use `genreName` consistently, but prefer aligning the struct to `name` to match the exercise description.
